---
title: "Sonic Pi cheat sheet"
---

The subset this book uses. The built-in help pane documents everything else, and
it is faster than any web search.

## Sound

| Call | Does |
|---|---|
| `play :c4` | Play a note. Accepts symbols or MIDI integers. |
| `play_chord [:c4, :e4, :g4]` | Play notes together. |
| `sample :bd_haus` | Play a recorded sample. |
| `use_synth :prophet` | Set the instrument for what follows. |
| `synth :pluck, note: :c4` | Play one note on a named synth without switching. |

Common `play` options:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `amp: 0.7` | Scale amplitude. Values above 1 are possible and can clip. |
| `pan: -0.5` | Place the sound left to right from -1 to 1. |
| `attack: 0.02` | Time taken to reach peak amplitude. |
| `decay: 0.1` | Time taken to move from the peak to sustain level. |
| `sustain: 0.4` | Time held at the sustain level. |
| `release: 0.6` | Fade time after sustain. |
| `cutoff: 90` | Low-pass filter cutoff expressed as a MIDI note number. |

`play` returns a synth node. `control` can change a running node when a lesson
needs a continuous bend or fade.

```ruby
voice = play :c4, sustain: 2, note_slide: 0.5
sleep 1
control voice, note: :g4
```

## Time

| Call | Does |
|---|---|
| `sleep 1` | Advance one beat. |
| `use_bpm 96` | Set the tempo. |
| `live_loop :name do ... end` | A named loop that runs concurrently and can be redefined while running. |
| `in_thread do ... end` | Run a block concurrently, once. |
| `sync :name` / `cue :name` | Wait for, and send, a start signal. |

One beat lasts `60.0 / bpm` seconds. Score durations stay in beats, so a tempo
change does not require rewriting them.

`at` schedules several offsets from the same starting point:

```ruby
at [0, 0.5, 1.5], [:c4, :e4, :g4] do |note|
  play note
end
sleep 2
```

## Patterns and state

| Call | Does |
|---|---|
| `ring(1, 2, 3)` | Build a circular sequence. |
| `pattern.tick` | Advance the current thread's counter and index the ring. |
| `pattern.look` | Read at the current counter without advancing. |
| `tick_reset` | Reset counters in the current thread. |
| `set :name, value` | Store named Sonic Pi state. |
| `get :name` | Read named Sonic Pi state. |

Counters belong to a thread. Two live loops can tick rings independently without
stealing positions from each other.

## Envelope

`attack`, `decay`, `sustain`, `release`, all in beats. `amp` scales loudness.
`pan` places the sound between -1 and 1.

The total audible lifetime often extends beyond the following `sleep`. `sleep`
advances the score cursor; envelope options describe the synth node. Long release
times therefore overlap later notes.

## Music helpers

| Call | Returns |
|---|---|
| `note(:c4)` | `60` |
| `note_info(:c4)` | A structure with name, octave, and MIDI number. |
| `scale(:c4, :major)` | A ring of the scale's notes. |
| `chord(:c4, :major)` | A ring of the chord's notes. |
| `chord_invert(chord(:c4, :major), 1)` | The chord, inverted. |
| `hz_to_midi(440)` / `midi_to_hz(69)` | Convert between frequency and note number. |

Rings returned by `scale` and `chord` support ordinary indexing and iteration.
Call `.to_a` when a plain array makes printed comparisons clearer.

## Samples

| Call | Does |
|---|---|
| `sample :bd_haus` | Trigger a built-in sample. |
| `sample_duration :loop_amen` | Return the sample length in seconds. |
| `sample :loop_amen, beat_stretch: 4` | Stretch a loop to four beats. |
| `sample :ambi_choir, rate: -1` | Play a sample backwards. |

Sample names are symbols. Use the completion menu or the built-in help rather
than relying on a name from a different Sonic Pi version.

## Randomness

`rrand(lo, hi)` for a float, `rrand_i(lo, hi)` for an integer, `choose` to pick
from a list, `one_in(n)` for a probability. Set `use_random_seed 42` at the top of any
example whose output should be reproducible.

Random calls made in separate threads follow separate deterministic streams.
Moving a random call into another loop can therefore change the result even when
the seed stays fixed.

## Effects

```ruby
with_fx :reverb, room: 0.8 do
  play :c4
end
```

`:reverb`, `:echo`, `:lpf`, `:hpf`, and `:distortion` cover almost everything this
book needs. Effects nest, and order changes the signal path.

```ruby
with_fx :distortion, distort: 0.2 do
  with_fx :reverb, room: 0.7 do
    play :e3, release: 2
  end
end
```

## Inspection and failure

| Call | Does |
|---|---|
| `puts value` | Print a value in the log. |
| `print value` | Print without adding a line break. |
| `raise "message"` | Stop the current run with an explicit error. |
| `assert condition` | Fail when a Sonic Pi assertion is false. |

Print score data before blaming a synth. For a missing note, inspect pitch,
onset, duration, and amplitude in that order. A duration or amplitude of zero can
look like a scheduler problem while the scheduler is behaving correctly.

## Fresh-buffer checklist

Before treating an example as self-contained, press Stop, switch to an unused
buffer, paste the block, and run it. Confirm that every `define`, variable, synth
selection, tempo, and random seed it requires appears above its first use. A
successful second run in a dirty buffer does not prove that condition.
